title: Giuoco Piano
intro: 3...Bc5: build the centre with 4.c3, then choose d3 or d4 by Black's reply.
variation: e2e4 e7e5 g1f3 b8c6 f1c4 f8c5

lessons.title: 4.c3 and the quiet plan
lessons.summary: c3, d3, castle and h3: a calm, solid set-up.

steps.text: Black answers with 3...Bc5, the Giuoco Piano. The bishop aims at f2, as yours aims at f7.
Prepare d4. Find the pawn move that lets a pawn take back on d4.
steps.hint: A pawn move on the queenside, next to your d-pawn.
steps.ifWrong: The plan is 4.c3, getting ready for d4.
steps.ifRight: 4.c3 prepares d4 and takes the d4 square from Black's knight.

feedback.d2d3: 4.d3 is fine too, but this repertoire plays 4.c3 first.
feedback.e1g1: Castling is fine, but this repertoire plays 4.c3 first to prepare d4.

steps.text: Black develops with 4...Nf6 and attacks your e4 pawn.
Protect e4 with a pawn. This repertoire keeps the centre closed for now.
steps.ifWrong: 5.d3 guards e4, so the knight cannot take it.
steps.ifRight: e4 is safe. Castle next, then think about a4, b4 or a slow d4.

feedback.d2d4: 5.d4 is the sharp old main line. This repertoire prefers the quiet 5.d3.

steps.text: 5...d6 supports e5 and opens a diagonal for the bishop on c8.
Make your king safe.
steps.ifWrong: Castle with 6.O-O. The rook can come to e1 later.
steps.ifRight: Next come h3, Re1 and Nbd2.

steps.text: Black castles too with 6...O-O. Both kings are safe and the centre is closed.
Black's bishop wants g4, to pin your knight to the queen. Stop it.
steps.hint: A rook's pawn can take g4 away.
steps.ifWrong: 7.h3 takes the g4 square from Black's bishop.
steps.ifRight: No pin. Re1 and Nbd2 can follow.

steps.text: Black played 6...h6 instead of castling. Your plan does not change. Find the move.
steps.hint: The same square still needs covering.
steps.ifRight: Re1 and Nbd2 come next, with no pin to worry about.

lessons.title: Against ...h6: b4 and a4
lessons.summary: When Black wastes a move, take space on the queenside.

steps.text: After 4.c3 Nf6 5.d3, Black can castle at once with 5...O-O.
Castle as well.
steps.ifRight: Both kings are safe. Now see what Black does.

steps.text: 6...h6 only stops Ng5 and Bg5. It does nothing in the centre, so you take space on the queenside.
Gain space and chase the bishop on c5.

feedback.h2h3: 7.h3 is playable, but 7.b4 gains space and attacks the bishop.

steps.text: 7...Bb6 keeps the bishop on its diagonal towards f2.
Threaten to trap the bishop on b6.
steps.ifWrong: 8.a4 threatens a5, and the bishop would have no good square.
steps.ifRight: Black usually makes room with ...a6 or ...a5.

steps.text: This came from the Two Knights: 3...Nf6 4.d3 Bc5 5.O-O O-O 6.c3 h6. Find your plan.
steps.hint: The same queenside pawn push as before.
steps.ifWrong: 7.b4 gains space and chases the bishop.
steps.ifRight: Same position, same plan: b4, then a4.

lessons.title: Against 4...d6: take the centre
lessons.summary: A passive reply lets you build a big centre with d4.

steps.text: 4...d6 is passive. It does not attack e4, so you can take the centre at once.
Strike in the centre now.
Black takes with 5...exd4.
Take back and keep two pawns in the centre.
steps.hint: Recapture with the pawn from c3.
steps.ifRight: Pawns on e4 and d4, and the bishop on c5 must move.

steps.text: 6...Bb4+ looks active. The bishop escapes with check.
Block the check with a piece that develops.
steps.ifWrong: 7.Nc3 blocks, develops, and guards e4 and d5.
steps.ifRight: Castle next. Later, d5 can gain more space.

feedback.c1d2: 7.Bd2 also blocks, but 7.Nc3 is stronger: it develops a new piece and guards e4 and d5.

steps.text: Black's other choice is 6...Bb6, keeping the bishop aimed at f2.
Your centre is safe. Bring your king to safety.
steps.ifWrong: 7.O-O: castle and keep the big centre.
steps.ifRight: Then h3 and Nc3. Later, d5 at the right moment pushes Black's pieces back.

steps.text: Back to 6...Bb4+. Block the check and develop a piece.
steps.hint: Use a knight, not the bishop.
steps.ifWrong: 7.Nc3 develops and guards e4 and d5.
steps.ifRight: The knight blocks the check and guards your centre.

feedback.c1d2: 7.Bd2 also blocks, but 7.Nc3 is stronger: it develops a new piece and guards e4 and d5.

lessons.title: Against 5...h6: h3 and Re1
lessons.summary: The same slow plan, with the rook behind e4.

steps.text: Black can also play 5...h6 first. It stops Ng5 and Bg5.
The plan stays the same. Castle.
steps.ifWrong: 6.O-O first. ...h6 changes nothing in the centre.

steps.text: 6...d6 supports e5 and frees the bishop on c8.
Stop the pin on your knight before it happens.
steps.ifRight: The knight on f3 can stay where it is.

steps.text: Black castles with 7...O-O.
Back up e4 with a rook.
steps.hint: The rook on f1 has a better square.
steps.ifWrong: 8.Re1 supports e4 and gets ready for d4 one day.

steps.text: Next the knight on b1 travels to d2, f1 and g3. d4 waits until you are ready.
This time Black castles: 5...h6 6.O-O O-O. Which queenside plan fits?
steps.ifWrong: 7.b4 gains space and attacks the bishop.
steps.ifRight: b4 and then a4, as against ...h6 before.
